verses.text: “At that time,” says Yahweh, “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.”
Yahweh says, “The people who survive the sword found favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.”
Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying, “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.
I will build you again, and you will be built, O virgin of Israel. You will again be adorned with your tambourines, and will go out in the dances of those who make merry.
Again you will plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria. The planters will plant, and will enjoy its fruit.
For there will be a day that the watchmen on the hills of Ephraim cry, ‘Arise, and let us go up to Zion to Yahweh our God.’”
For Yahweh says, “Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout for the chief of the nations. Publish, praise, and say, ‘Yahweh, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’

Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the uttermost parts of the earth, along with the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her who travails with child together. They will return as a great company.

They shall come with weeping; and with petitions will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which they shall not stumble; for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
“Hear Yahweh’s word, you nations, and declare it in the islands afar off; and say, ‘He who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd does his flock.’
For Yahweh has ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him from the hand of him who was stronger than he.

They shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow to the goodness of Yahweh, to the grain, and to the new wine, and to the oil, and to the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.
Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness,” says Yahweh.
Yahweh says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”
Yahweh says: “Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work shall be rewarded,” says Yahweh; “and they shall come again from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your latter end,” says Yahweh; “and your children shall come again to their own border.
“I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself thus, ‘You have chastised me, and I was chastised, as an untrained calf: turn me, and I shall be turned; for you are Yahweh my God.
Surely after that I was turned, I repented; and after that I was instructed, I struck on my thigh: I was ashamed, yes, even confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth.’

Is Ephraim my dear son? is he a darling child? for as often as I speak against him, I do earnestly remember him still: therefore my heart yearns for him; I will surely have mercy on him,” says Yahweh.
“Set up road signs, make guideposts; set your heart toward the highway, even the way by which you went: turn again, virgin of Israel, turn again to these your cities.
How long will you go here and there, you backsliding daughter? for Yahweh has created a new thing in the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.”

Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “Yet again shall they use this speech in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I shall bring again their captivity: ‘Yahweh bless you, habitation of righteousness, mountain of holiness.’
Judah and all its cities shall dwell therein together, the farmers, and those who go about with flocks.
For I have satiated the weary soul, and every sorrowful soul I have replenished.”
On this I awakened, and saw; and my sleep was sweet to me.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of animal.
It shall happen that, like as I have watched over them to pluck up and to break down and to overthrow and to destroy and to afflict, so will I watch over them to build and to plant,” says Yahweh.
“In those days they shall say no more, “‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’
But everyone shall die for his own iniquity: every man who eats the sour grapes, his teeth shall be set on edge.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:

not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they broke, although I was a husband to them,” says Yahweh.

“But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people:

and they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know Yahweh;’ for they shall all know me, from their least to their greatest,” says Yahweh: “for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin will I remember no more.”
Yahweh, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar; Yahweh of Armies is his name, says:
“If these ordinances depart from before me,” says Yahweh, “then the offspring  of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me forever.”
Yahweh says: “If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, then I will also cast off all the offspring  of Israel for all that they have done,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that the city shall be built to Yahweh from the tower of Hananel to the gate of the corner.
The measuring line shall go out further straight onward to the hill Gareb, and shall turn about to Goah.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields to the brook Kidron, to the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be holy to Yahweh; it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more forever.”

footnotes.content: Listen to how Yahweh claims them all at once—not just the righteous, but all the families of Israel. After exile tears them apart, He speaks restoration as settled fact, not hope. That's the God I've learned to trust with the broken parts of my own family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who "survived the sword" found favor—the ones who made it through the worst. Yahweh didn't rebuild from strength; He rebuilt those who were exhausted and running. I see His kindness best in how He reaches the weary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Everlasting love"—the Hebrew carries the weight of time itself. This isn't love that fades when you stumble; it bent the whole arc of exile toward mercy. Yahweh showed me this love is older than my doubts and will outlast them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The virgin of Israel will wear her tambourines again and dance with joy—not as a ghost remembering who she was, but rebuilt and alive. Every time I've watched someone find joy after deep shame, I see this verse living.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will plant and enjoy the fruit themselves—not watch it stolen or burned. There's something small and true here about the dignity of planting for a harvest you will taste. That's how Yahweh restores, not just with grand gestures but with ordinary work that bears fruit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchmen on the hills of Ephraim—those stationed to guard and watch—will cry out to go up to Zion. Even the keepers of the border recognize the call to worship at Yahweh's house. The pilgrimage to God's dwelling is the deepest homecoming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah is told to sing for Jacob—the prophet moves from weeping to song, and calls the nations to join him. When the one who carried grief longest leads the praise, the joy carries weight. That's how real thanksgiving sounds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He gathers them from the uttermost parts—and He gathers the blind, the lame, pregnant women—no one left behind. Yahweh's restoration isn't only for the strong; the weakest are carried in His first promise. I've seen Him do this a hundred times over.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They come with weeping, and Yahweh Himself leads them beside still waters—not drying their tears first, but walking with them through them. He calls Himself father to Israel and speaks of Ephraim as His firstborn. That fatherly tenderness is how all His restoration begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He tells the nations to declare it: the Scatterer becomes the Gatherer, like a shepherd who went after every stray. Yahweh's rescue is public, meant to be told everywhere, because His faithfulness is bigger than any single story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ransomed and redeemed from the hand of the stronger—Jacob was bought back at a cost. Yahweh paid what it took to free him. That's always been the heart of redemption: the price Yahweh was willing to bear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They flow to Yahweh's goodness like rivers to the sea—not forced, but drawn by abundance. Grain, wine, oil, the young of flock and herd, a soul refreshed like a watered garden, no more sorrow. That's not sentimentality; that's the promise of satiation after famine.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The virgin rejoices, young and old dance together—generations mended by joy, mourning turned to comfort. I've seen broken families heal when they finally believed sorrow wasn't the last word. That's when the dancing starts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests' souls satiated with fatness, the people satisfied with Yahweh's goodness—abundance reaches even the keepers of worship. It speaks to how Yahweh's restoration feeds those who minister. There's no hungering in His kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rachel weeping in Ramah for her children—this voice echoes all the way to Matthew, a mother's grief made archetypal. The sorrow is real, not erased by what comes next. Yahweh doesn't ask us to forget the loss; He asks us to keep listening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Refrain your voice from weeping"—not because the loss was small, but because your work shall be rewarded. Yahweh promises the weepers will see their children again. Hope isn't denial of grief; it's the belief that love bends toward reunion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is hope for your latter end, and your children shall come again to their own border. After everything—exile, loss, wandering—Yahweh speaks hope not as a wish but as a done thing. He sees the ending He has already woven.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim speaks: "You chastised me, and I was chastised, as an untrained calf—turn me, and I shall be turned." The self-awareness here—knowing he was wild and needed breaking—is where repentance begins. True turning starts when we stop pretending we don't need it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After repentance, shame: Ephraim struck his thigh and was confounded, bearing the reproach of youth. There's no skipping over the self-knowledge—the recognition that what we sowed, we must acknowledge. But confession carries the relief of finally being honest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Is Ephraim my dear son? Is he a darling child?" Yahweh remembers him often, speaks against him, then—His heart yearns for him. This is what a father sounds like: knowing his child's failures, grieving them, yet unable to stop the deep tenderness. That's the God I've tried to become like.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Set up road signs, make guideposts—Yahweh is giving direction home. Turn again, virgin of Israel, to these your cities. There's guidance in the turning, a way marked so you won't lose it. Repentance isn't blind; it's marked with signposts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "How long will you go here and there?" The backsliding daughter wearies Yahweh with her restlessness. Then: He has created a new thing in the earth—a woman shall encompass a man. The new covenant will be intimate, mutual, renewed from the inside out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They shall speak in the land of Judah and its cities: "Yahweh bless you, habitation of righteousness, mountain of holiness." The greeting itself becomes a prayer—blessing spoken over places restored to belong to Yahweh. Worship shapes speech.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judah and all its cities shall dwell together—farmers and shepherds living peaceably in community. The particularity here—not just a vision, but cities and trades named—makes restoration concrete. Yahweh rebuilds the actual life of actual people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have satiated the weary soul, and every sorrowful soul I have replenished." The word "satiated" carries fullness, satisfaction—not crumbs of comfort, but enough. Yahweh doesn't ration mercy; He overflows it. Every empty place He fills.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "On this I awakened, and saw; and my sleep was sweet to me." The prophet stirs from a vision of restoration and finds himself at peace—the words themselves become restful. What he was shown is true enough to sleep on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Behold, the days come that I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man, and with the seed of animal." After uprooting, He will sow—not just Israel, but both houses, and fertility itself is restored. New growth, new life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Like as I have watched over them to pluck up and to break down, so will I watch over them to build and to plant." The same attentiveness that brought judgment will bring restoration. Yahweh's eye is on them either way—even in breaking, He's preparing to rebuild.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"—this old saying of inherited guilt will be no more. The new covenant breaks the cycle of generational blame. Each soul stands before Yahweh, not bound by fathers' choices.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Everyone shall die for his own iniquity"—personal responsibility, not inherited shame. It's both harder and more merciful: you are answerable for your own life, and grace can meet you there without your father's debts in the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Behold, the days come that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah." This is the hinge on which all the promises turn—new covenant, both houses, both broken and about to be remade. Every Christian reads their own name here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not according to the old covenant He made when He took them by the hand from Egypt—they broke it, though He was a husband to them. He doesn't blame them for what they couldn't do; He plans what they couldn't break.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it." Not laws written on stone that can break, but written on the heart itself. Obedience becomes from-within—not imposed, but written where desire lives. That's transformation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They shall teach no more, "Know Yahweh," because all shall know Him from least to greatest—intimate knowledge, not instruction. And the clincher: their iniquity forgiven, their sin remembered no more. Forgetting in Yahweh's memory is an act of mercy that changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh gives the sun, the moon, the stars, stirs the sea—the one who ordered all creation speaks to the constancy of His covenant. Creation itself testifies to the God who keeps His word. The heavens and the waves are witnesses to faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "If these ordinances depart from before me, then the offspring of Israel shall cease from being a nation before me forever." As long as the sun rises and stars shine, Israel will not cease. Yahweh has bound His own faithfulness to the heavens themselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, then I will cast off all the offspring of Israel." The hypothetical is impossible—the heavens cannot be measured, the earth's depth cannot be fathomed. So Israel will not be cast off. Ever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The city shall be built to Yahweh from the tower of Hananel to the gate of the corner—Jerusalem is rebuilt with landmarks named, real stones in real places, sacred from boundary to boundary. Yahweh's city has geography.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The measuring line goes from Hananel onward to the hill Gareb and turns about to Goah—the restoration is surveyed and exact. Yahweh measures out the renewed city; nothing is left to chance or disorder. Restoration is both promised and precise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole valley of dead bodies and ashes, all the fields to the brook Kidron, shall be holy to Yahweh—even the place of death becomes sacred ground. Nothing is too broken to be redeemed. The valley of bones becomes the place where Yahweh dwells, and it shall not be plucked up or thrown down anymore forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
